clue.text: As harbinger of spring — the avalanche

definitions.meaning: a small white flower that blooms in late winter, heralding the new season
read literally, a fall or drop of snow down a mountainside

explanation.surface: A poetic line hailing the first sign of spring as a mountain slide.
explanation.definitionFit: The flower is a traditional herald of spring, and an avalanche is literally a downward plunge of snow.

clue.text: Our remedy being the prohibition of sloppy play?

parts.note: a ban is expressed by the single word no
to strum is to play a guitar casually or carelessly

explanation.surface: A tongue-in-cheek cure: banning careless music-making.
explanation.walkthrough: The word is Latin for 'our', so 'Our remedy' is a fair, learned definition of a pet cure.
explanation.definitionFit: A quack medicine, originally a remedy its maker called 'ours', a pet panacea.

clue.text: Universal description of this oblate spheroid

definitions.meaning: the earth, a flattened sphere, is broad at its equator: a planet that is broad

explanation.surface: A geography lesson describing the shape of the earth.
explanation.definitionFit: Universal means global in reach; the second reading jokingly describes our planet as broad.

clue.text: Right to raise spirits? So people tell

parts.note: to elate is to cheer someone up

explanation.surface: Is it proper to cheer people up? So folk say.
explanation.definitionFit: To recount or narrate a story is to tell it.

clue.text: Plain sailing for young men going west in this?

definitions.text: young men going west in this

parts.note: a prairie is a broad grassy plain of North America
a schooner is a sailing vessel

explanation.surface: An easy voyage for youthful pioneers heading for the frontier.
explanation.walkthrough: The clue echoes 'Go west, young man'; the answer is the covered wagon of American settlers, likened to a ship crossing a sea of grass.
explanation.definitionFit: The canvas-topped wagon that carried settlers across the American plains westward.

clue.text: Change in first class post in a manner of speaking

indicators.note: the letters are to be altered into a fresh order

parts.note: A1, written AI, means first-rate
taken as written

explanation.surface: Altering the arrangements for premium mail delivery, figuratively speaking.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Change' rearranges AI (A1, first class) with POST.
explanation.definitionFit: A regional dialect is a local way of talking.

clue.text: Proudhon's theft

parts.note: the French anarchist Proudhon famously declared that owning things is itself theft

explanation.surface: A reference to a famous anarchist slogan.
explanation.walkthrough: Pierre-Joseph Proudhon wrote 'What is property? Property is theft!'
explanation.definitionFit: Ownership, the thing Proudhon branded as stealing.

clue.text: When 'Poe in mid-fall-remembered Ulalume

parts.note: Poe's poem Ulalume is set on a night in the lonesome tenth month of the year

explanation.surface: Asks at what season Poe recalled his lost Ulalume.
explanation.walkthrough: Poe's 'Ulalume' opens 'It was night in the lonesome' tenth month; 'mid-fall' is autumn in American usage.
explanation.definitionFit: The month in the middle of autumn, when Poe's poem is set.

clue.text: As such, the prodigal son envied his charges' diet

definitions.text: As such, the prodigal son envied his charges' diet

parts.words: As such, the prodigal son envied his charges' diet
parts.note: in the parable the wasteful son, reduced to tending pigs, longed to eat their husks

explanation.surface: A Bible story: the prodigal son coveting what his animals ate.
explanation.walkthrough: In Luke 15 the prodigal son, hired to feed pigs, would gladly have eaten their pods.
explanation.definitionFit: A keeper of pigs, which is the job the prodigal son took.

clue.text: Would this plane achieve the ends of the RAF?

definitions.text: Would this plane achieve the ends of the RAF?

parts.words: Would this plane achieve the ends of the RAF?
parts.note: the RAF motto is Per ardua ad astra, 'through adversity to the stars', so its goal is the starry plane

explanation.surface: Wonders whether an aircraft could fulfil the air force's aims.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Plane' suggests an aircraft but means a level of existence; the RAF's motto aims at the stars.
explanation.definitionFit: Relating to the stars, the realm of a mystical higher plane.

clue.text: Loves a more abstinent one

parts.note: taken as written
TT means teetotal, abstaining from alcohol
I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: Comparing romances: one who abstains more.
explanation.definitionFit: Cupids, little winged figures of love in art.

clue.text: Believe gold will satisfy him?

parts.note: to credit a statement is to believe it
or is the heraldic word for gold

explanation.surface: Trust that money will pay off the man you owe.
explanation.definitionFit: The person owed a debt is the one appeased by payment in gold.

clue.text: Authorize rejection of the Spanish poison

indicators.note: rejection throws back, so the pieces are read backwards

parts.note: el is Spanish for the
bane is an old word for poison

explanation.surface: Sanctioning a refusal of Spanish toxin.
explanation.definitionFit: To empower or permit someone is to authorize them.

clue.text: A cockfight at full speed

parts.note: a main is a series of matches in cockfighting

explanation.surface: A bird fight racing along.
explanation.definitionFit: An archaic adverb meaning with full force or haste.

clue.text: Movement is slowish-and not in a whirl

indicators.note: the words are spun about in a whirl, so their letters are reordered

explanation.surface: A dance that is slowish, not frantic.
explanation.definitionFit: A musical term for a passage played at a moderately slow pace, a little quicker than andante.

clue.text: Supporters to: back English, leader in the green hillside

parts.note: vert is the heraldic word for green
brae is Scottish for a hillside

explanation.surface: Advice to back an English leader on a green slope.
explanation.walkthrough: The colon is a misprint in the scanned text. 'leader in the' places E ahead of BRAE.
explanation.definitionFit: The bones of the spine hold up the human frame along its length.

clue.text: Two 'of the things : Paganini needed for execution

parts.note: a violinist like Paganini needs a bow and strings
a violinist like Paganini needs a bow and strings

explanation.surface: The violinist Paganini's tools for performing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'execution' suggests performance, but a bowstring was used by Ottoman executioners to strangle.
explanation.definitionFit: The Ottoman method of strangling the condemned used a cord from a bow.

clue.text: Drake's period for geologists

definitions.meaning: Sir Francis Drake was a native of the English county of Devon
a geological period of the Palaeozoic era

explanation.surface: The era of Drake, as a geologist might date it.
explanation.definitionFit: Drake was a Devon man; the name also labels a geological period of fishes, named for Devon rocks.

clue.text: Due to Pooh-Bah as a man of pedigree

definitions.text: Due to Pooh-Bah as a man of pedigree

parts.words: Due to Pooh-Bah as a man of pedigree
parts.note: Pooh-Bah in The Mikado is proud of his ancient lineage and expects respect

explanation.surface: The respect owed to a proud aristocrat.
explanation.walkthrough: Pooh-Bah is Gilbert and Sullivan's haughty official with pre-Adamite ancestry.
explanation.definitionFit: Respectful submission is what a proud noble expects.

clue.text: Needed to help, keep staff in ancestral home

indicators.note: the words keep the answer held inside them

explanation.surface: Money needed to retain servants in the family seat.
explanation.walkthrough: 'keep' signals letters held inside 'staff in ancestral'; 'home' completes the picture.
explanation.definitionFit: Money or funding is what is required to support a venture.

clue.text: Return attractions for the turf

indicators.note: a return sends the word back, read from the end

parts.note: draws are things that attract crowds

explanation.surface: Bringing back the crowd-pullers to the racecourse.
explanation.definitionFit: A grassy expanse or lawn.

clue.text: What to do if thrown — another horse?

definitions.meaning: get back in the saddle after a fall
a fresh mount supplied to a rider

explanation.surface: Riding advice after a fall.
explanation.definitionFit: Climbing back on is the remedy for a fall; a fresh mount is a replacement steed.

clue.text: One to draw the line — police constable perhaps

indicators.note: perhaps signals the letters may be arranged otherwise

explanation.surface: Someone who sets boundaries, such as a policeman.
explanation.definitionFit: A writing tool used for sketching.

clue.text: Sister I put in business as Pope's. representative

parts.note: a nun is a religious sister

indicators.note: put in places one piece inside another

parts.note: CO is the abbreviation for company

explanation.surface: A nun given a role in the Vatican's affairs.
explanation.definitionFit: A papal envoy or ambassador.

clue.text: Public unit gets me more pay-for this work

parts.note: overt means done openly
I is the Roman numeral one, a single unit

explanation.surface: Extra money for extra labour.
explanation.definitionFit: Hours beyond the normal shift earn extra wages.

clue.text: Open road with this key?

parts.note: turning a car's starting key lets you set off down the highway

explanation.surface: A key that unlocks the open road.
explanation.walkthrough: 'key' suggests a door key, but it is the one that starts the car.
explanation.definitionFit: The starting mechanism of a car engine.

clue.text: One old golf-club, say, or a set

indicators.note: say signals the word is spoken

parts.note: a cleek is an old iron golf club

explanation.surface: An antique golf club, or a set of them.
explanation.walkthrough: A CLEEK was an early iron club; said aloud it matches the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: An exclusive group of people.

clue.text: His love-in-idleness had magic power

parts.note: in A Midsummer Night's Dream the fairy king uses the flower love-in-idleness as a love potion

explanation.surface: A man whose lazy romance worked wonders.
explanation.walkthrough: Love-in-idleness is a pansy whose juice makes sleepers fall in love in Shakespeare's play.
explanation.definitionFit: The fairy king in Shakespeare who wields the flower's charm.

clue.text: Concerning ambassador put in lower position

parts.note: re means about or concerning
a legate is an envoy

explanation.surface: An envoy demoted.
explanation.definitionFit: To demote or consign to a lesser rank.
